chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding

a man said to another, 'Sell me the fruit of your palm tree, this one that is in it, for two Qafeez of dates, or less than that, or more, naming whatever he wishes.' So he sold it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The dates and the unripened dates from a single palm tree are one; there is no problem with it. But if one mixes the old dates and the unripened dates, it is not valid; and the raisins and the grapes are like that.'

key_terms.بِقَفِيزَيْنِ: For two Qafeez (a unit of volume measurement)

ai.seo_question: What is the validity of selling palm fruit based on an estimated quantity of dates?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the rules of *Riba al-Fadl* (excess in exchange) within the context of *Bay' al-Mu'atharah* (barter), specifically addressing the sale of unripened fruit (*Busr*) for dried fruit (*Tamr*) based on estimated volume (*Qafeez*). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between permissible sales of produce from the same tree and invalid sales involving mixed qualities or stages of ripeness, such as old dates with new ones, ensuring transparency and preventing uncertainty (*Gharar*). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on precise measurement and homogeneity in commodity exchanges to maintain economic justice.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who said to another, ‘Sell the dates of your palm tree to me, this one in which they are, with two Qafeez (a unit of measurement) of dates, or less than that, or more, naming whatever you so desires to’. So he sells it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The dates and the unripened dates from a palm tree are one, there is no problem with it. But if you were to mix the old dates and the unripened, so it is not correct; and the raisins and the grapes are like that’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “About the case of a man who asks another man to sell the fruits of his certain palm tree for two Qafiz (a certain unit of measurement) of dates or less or more that he names as he likes, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is not harmful.’

He (the Imam) then said, ‘Fresh dates and half-ripe dates from one palm tree can be exchanged and it is not harmful but mixing of old dates and half-ripe dates is not valid and so also is the case of raisin and grape.’”
